name: The scribes and Pharisees
charge: Shutting up the kingdom against men; devouring widows' houses; tithing mint and omitting judgment, mercy and faith; whited sepulchres
summary: They sat in Moses' seat and were to be heard; their works were not to be followed. Eight woes in Matthew 23 name the crimes, and the sentence at the end gathers all the righteous blood from Abel to Zacharias on that generation: your house is left unto you desolate.
offense: They bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers. Ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men. Ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer. Ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith. Ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones. Ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.
judgment: Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell? Behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias. Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation. Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. Forty years later the house was.

entries.commentary: The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat. Whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works, for they say, and do not. They bind heavy burdens and lay them on men's shoulders, but will not move them with one of their fingers.

All their works they do for to be seen of men. They love the uppermost rooms at feasts and the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the markets. He that is greatest among you shall be your servant. Whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased, and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.

Woe unto you: ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men, for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in. They devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer, and shall receive the greater damnation. There is a lesson in what they would not do. Where leadership provokes a man to works and he finds himself falling behind, he should take it to heart, because telling people who they are without putting in the labour yields no fruit.

They compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and make him twofold more the child of hell than themselves. Their rules about swearing by the gold rather than the temple, and by the gift rather than the altar, are called out as blindness: the temple sanctifies the gold and the altar sanctifies the gift.

They pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin and have omitted the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy, and faith. These ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.

They make clean the outside of the cup and platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Cleanse first that which is within. They are likened unto whited sepulchres, beautiful outward but within full of dead men's bones. Outwardly they appear righteous unto men, but within are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

They build the tombs of the prophets and say they would not have shed their blood, and by saying it they witness against themselves that they are the children of them which killed the prophets. Upon them comes all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias. This is the plainest speaking in the gospel. Christ was no soft man with these teachers of the law who did not believe it.
O Jerusalem, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not. Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples. He gives them the words: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

The friend at midnight will not rise because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth. Importunity is persistence to the point of annoyance. The man kept knocking, and the man inside gave him enough that he would not come back.

Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you. The parable before it is the point: prayer is not said once and left. There is persistence in it, and there is action behind it, because the man in the parable was standing at the door. If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?
He casts out a devil, and it was dumb, and when the devil was gone out the dumb spake, and the people wondered. Others said he cast out devils through Beelzebub.

Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. If Satan also be divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? If I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges. But if I with the finger of God cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you.

When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, his goods are in peace; but when a stronger than he shall come upon him, he taketh from him all his armour and divideth his spoils. He that is not with me is against me: and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.

The unclean spirit returns and finds the house swept and garnished, and takes seven other spirits more wicked than himself. The house was clean and empty. There was no stronger one dwelling in it, and that is why what came back could enter, and the last state of that man is worse than the first.
A woman blesses the womb that bare him, and he answers, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it. He turned honour away from the mother and onto the keeping of the word.

This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet. The queen of the south came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and a greater than Solomon is here. The men of Nineveh repented at the preaching of Jonas, and a greater than Jonas is here. Men came a long way for less than what these would not cross the room for.

The light of the body is the eye: when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when thine eye is evil, thy body also is full of darkness. One lamp lights a whole room, and put out, the whole room is dark. An eye fixed on the word fills the man with light; an eye that goes looking in dark places fills the whole man, thoughts and judgments together, with darkness.

Ye Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and the platter; but your inward part is full of ravening and wickedness. Ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets, and ye are as graves which appear not.

One of the lawyers says, Master, thus saying thou reproachest us also, and is answered with a woe of his own. Ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers. Ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and your fathers killed them, so ye bear witness that ye allow the deeds of your fathers. The blood of all the prophets, shed from the foundation of the world, from the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, shall be required of this generation. Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.
The scribes and Pharisees began to urge him vehemently, laying wait for him, and seeking to catch something out of his mouth, that they might accuse him. From that point they were done with him.

Woe to Ariel, the city where David dwelt; Ariel means lion of God, and this is spoken to Israel, to Jerusalem. Year to year they add and kill sacrifices, yet He will distress Ariel with heaviness and sorrow. He will encamp against her round about and lay siege, bringing the nations around because of Israel's sins, and she shall be brought down to speak low out of the ground, her voice like one that hath a familiar spirit whispering out of the dust.

The multitude of her strangers shall be like small dust and the terrible ones as chaff that passes away suddenly; she shall be visited of the Lord of hosts with thunder, earthquake, great noise, storm, tempest, and devouring fire, for Israel is contending against the Most High as well as the nations He brings. The multitude of nations that fight against Ariel shall be as a dream of a night vision: like a hungry man who dreams he eats but awakes empty, or a thirsty man who dreams he drinks but awakes faint. The nations dream of destroying Israel, but it shall not come to pass, though it will still be like a nightmare to His people. -

They are drunken but not with wine; their spiritual eyes are closed in a deep sleep of blindness, unable to see the things of the Bible. Before coming to the truth many thought Esau was actually white, until the scriptures showed by his description that he is red, showing how deep the spiritual sleep runs. The vision is become as the words of a book that is sealed: delivered to the learned who says he cannot read it because it is sealed, and to the unlearned who says he is not learned. Today's pastors say Revelation is still sealed, but it is sealed only to them, not to the righteous; many learn only how to mimic and perform from the television.

This people draw near with their mouth and honour Him with their lips but have removed their heart far from Him; they praise God but when [Deuteronomy 22:5](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v5) comes out they will not do it, for their fear toward Him is taught by the precepts of men, by the oppressors. Therefore He will do a marvellous work, and the wisdom of their wise men, the oppressors and mainly Esau, shall perish. Woe to them that seek deep to hide their counsel from the Most High and work in the dark saying, Who seeth us? Their turning of things upside down shall be esteemed as the potter's clay, for the Most High is setting His people back in order, turning right side up what Esau turned upside down. -

Yet a little while and Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field; in that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book, and the deaf are Israel, in a spiritual deep sleep now beginning to wake and hear the word of God rightly. The eyes of the blind shall see out of their obscurity, and the blind are Israel, like the obscurity of thinking Esau is white when he is red; the meek shall increase their joy in the Most High. -

The poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel, the poor in spirit, which is us; the terrible one and the scorner, Esau, is brought to naught and consumed, and all that watch for iniquity are cut off, including Israelites who love the oppressor with all their heart. Concerning the house of Jacob, the Most High who redeemed Abraham says Jacob shall not be ashamed nor his face wax pale; when he sees his children they shall sanctify His name and fear the God of Israel, and they that erred in spirit shall come to understanding and they that murmured shall learn doctrine. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.
Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also.
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.
Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous,

Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.
Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.

Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:

Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.

Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
And the Lord said unto him, Now do ye Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and the platter; but your inward part is full of ravening and wickedness.
Ye fools, did not he that made that which is without make that which is within also?
But rather give alms of such things as ye have; and, behold, all things are clean unto you.
But woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.
Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets.
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are as graves which appear not, and the men that walk over them are not aware of them.
Then answered one of the lawyers, and said unto him, Master, thus saying thou reproachest us also.
And he said, Woe unto you also, ye lawyers! for ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.
Woe unto you! for ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
Truly ye bear witness that ye allow the deeds of your fathers: for they indeed killed them, and ye build their sepulchres.
Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they shall slay and persecute:
That the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;
From the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, which perished between the altar and the temple: verily I say unto you, It shall be required of this generation.
Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.

Wherefore the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men:

Therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.
